svg.title: What fearless concurrency guarantees and what it does not
svg.desc: Left column lists what the Rust compiler rejects at compile time: data races, sending non thread safe types, borrowing locals that a thread could outlive, and touching lock-protected data without the lock. Right column lists bugs that still compile: deadlocks, check-then-act logic races, starvation, contention, and weak atomic orderings that break your own invariants.
svg.text: "Fearless concurrency" has a precise scope
Safe Rust rules out undefined behavior from shared memory. It does not prove your program is correct.
Rejected at compile time
Data races on ordinary memory
&mut XOR &, enforced across threads
Moving Rc or Cell into another thread
E0277: Send / Sync not implemented
Threads outliving borrowed locals
E0373: use move, Arc, or thread::scope
Reading guarded data without the lock
Mutex<T> owns T; the guard is the only door
Compiles fine, still your job
Deadlocks
A locks then B, B locks then A
Logic races (check, then act)
Each step locked, the pair is not atomic
Contention, starvation, livelock
Correct but slow; one hot lock serializes all
Too-weak atomic orderings
No UB, but other threads may see stale state
Also: leaks (Arc cycles), panics in workers
Design rule: make shared state small, keep critical sections short, and prefer message passing for ownership handoff.
